properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-17, supplying a taxonomy of AI-coding-agent pitfalls: "here are some other pitfalls I've seen that we should really weave into the fabric of reflow2 to prevent."

⭐ THE TRIAGE IS THE CONTRIBUTION, NOT THE LIST. reflow2 is a design graph and a coherence engine. It is not a linter, a package resolver, a type checker or a test runner. Recording "reflow2 prevents hallucinated packages" would be reflow2 claiming a capability it cannot have — which is `epoch:instruments-stop-overstating` committed by the very act of writing down the cure for it. So the list splits three ways and the split is what has to be decided before anything is built.

═══ CLASS A — REFLOW2 ALREADY DOES THIS. The move is to SAY SO, not to build again.
• "Tunnel vision: fixing a bug in one file silently breaks a dependency in another" — this is `propagate_change` and the impact-check skill, and it is reflow2's single most central competence. The blast radius exists for exactly this.
• "Context drift: as the conversation grows longer the agent forgets earlier architectural constraints" — the graph IS the memory outside the context window; `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` is the same finding already accepted.
• "Design bloat: dozens of unnecessary patterns, interfaces and abstractions" — an abstraction nothing asked for is `unmotivated_capability`, an existing gap; `granularity_report` reports the design/build mismatch in both directions.
• "Blind compliance: the agent implements your flawed logic instead of questioning it" — PARTLY. `detect_gaps` putting questions to the human, `CONTRADICTS` with its `contradiction` detector, and `dec:three-party-checks` ("the LLM speaks, the graph remembers and counts, the human decides") are the answer to the fraction of this that is a NEW requirement conflicting with a SETTLED one. The rest of it — a flaw with nothing in the graph to contradict — is Class C.

═══ CLASS B — REFLOW2 COULD REACH THIS AND CURRENTLY DOES NOT. The real candidate work.
• OSCILLATION — "agents get stuck repeatedly adding and removing the exact same line". Computable from checksum history: a value returning to a previous one is a loop. MEASURED AND BOUNDED — see `dec:idea-an-artifact-whose-checksum-returns-is-an-agent-going-in-circles`; the history is far too thin today to support it.
• MUTATION-PROOF ON A CHECK — "hollow test suites", "tautological testing", and his own best practice "mutate code to test tests". reflow2 CANNOT read an assertion and judge it tautological. It CAN record whether anybody PROVED the check can fail. Its own practice already does this informally and in prose: `ver:search-first-forces-a-choice` records "MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS, each verified applied before running rather than assumed" and then, remarkably, "A FOURTH MUTATION EXPOSED A VACUOUS TEST OF MY OWN" — reflow2 caught its own hollow test by mutation, and had nowhere structured to put that fact. ⇒ This is a candidate SHARPENING of `req:a-finding-has-somewhere-to-put-its-evidence` (accepted, epoch:instruments-stop-overstating) rather than a new requirement: the evidence field that requirement asks for is exactly where "this check was proven able to fail" belongs.
• A DEPENDENCY THE DESIGN NEVER DECLARED — the reachable half of "ghost packages". reflow2 cannot know whether `numpy.frobnicate()` exists, but `declare_dependency` / `reconcile_dependencies` can say that the build imports something the design never named. That catches the invented-dependency case at the design boundary while claiming nothing about the registry.

═══ CLASS C — REFLOW2 CAN NEVER DO THIS, AND MUST SAY SO RATHER THAN IMPLY IT.
• Whether a library method or package EXISTS (a resolver/language-server job).
• Whether an API is DEPRECATED (a registry/changelog job).
• Whether an assertion is TAUTOLOGICAL, or a mock has hollowed the path out (reading code semantically).
• Whether YOUR LOGIC IS FLAWED when nothing in the design contradicts it.
• Strict typing — a build-tool choice. It could be a DesignRule a project adopts; it is not something reflow2 can enforce or check.
⇒ These belong in reflow2's design ONLY as stated non-goals. A tool that lets a user believe it is watching for hallucinated packages has done more harm than one that says plainly it is not.

📌 AND THE ONE THAT CUTS ACROSS ALL THREE: "review diffs, not files; never accept a full-file rewrite blindly." reflow2 has the design-graph analogue ALREADY and learned it the hard way TODAY — `create_node`'s `revision` block names the properties a write replaced and their prior values, which is what caught this session overwriting a Decision's history. The open question is whether that is enough, or whether the same discipline should reach the artifact layer.
properties.name: OPEN — of the known AI-agent failure modes, which can reflow2 actually reach? Three classes, and writing the third into its design would be the overstating failure itself
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming. The triage is the contribution: reflow2 already answers four of these, could reach three more, and can never reach five. Writing the last five into its design as things it prevents would be the exact overstating failure this whole increment exists to end — a tool that lets a user believe it is watching for hallucinated packages has done more harm than one that says plainly it is not.
